name: Aave ParaSwap adapters retain allowances across mismatched swaps
summary: The repay adapter approved the declared collateral token but accepted Augustus calldata selecting a different token. A first successful swap funded the debt repayment without spending that collateral, leaving its allowance live. A later call declared another collateral asset while spending the previously approved token, bypassing checks limited to the current asset pair and draining DAO-owned residual balances in the adapter.

loss.notes: Components measure only the retained Ethereum transaction, summing token Transfer inflows minus outflows at the adapter; attacker collateral deposits/withdrawals and debt-repayment inputs cancel. Stablecoins use par; wstETH/WETH use pre-exploit Aave Oracle USD prices. The one-wei USDC and USDT differences between final attacker payouts and adapter depletion are not added to victim loss. Aave Labs final report gives $95,284.44 across repay-with-collateral and debt-switch adapters on multiple networks, superseding the preliminary $56,000 estimate. Those additional transactions, artifact/fault grouping and valuations remain unresolved, so the Ethereum subtotal is a lower bound, not a complete curve loss.

ageReset.description: Direct deployment; whether subsequent Augustus routing or registry changes were necessary to the fault remains unresolved.

limitations: Direct artifact identity and creation are reproduced; complete Augustus routing and registry history and their causal relevance remain unresolved.
The retained Ethereum transaction is confirmed exploitation; earliest successful use across affected adapter artifacts has not been established.

sources.note: Verified deployed source retrieved from https://etherscan.io/address/0x02e7b8511831b1b02d9018215a0f8f500ea5c6b3#code. Runtime identity and semantic inspection are documented in source-7.

Bounded semantic review reproduced eth_getTransactionReceipt and debug_traceTransaction with callTracer for source-1 and source-5. Creation is CREATE2 by 0x2401ae9bbef67458362710f90302eb52b5ce835a; the earlier note confused transaction sender with creator. eth_getCode is empty at 17678214 and has the recorded hash at 17678215 and 20624703. Exploit execution calls the adapter directly. Verified BaseParaSwapBuyAdapter._buyOnParaSwap reverts failed Augustus calls and checks current input/output balances; its flaw is persistent approval plus calldata that can spend another asset. In source-1, fake swaps leave allowances, subsequent calls use one satoshi WBTC as declared collateral while spending earlier approved wstETH/USDC/WETH/USDT through Augustus. Receipt Transfer logs at the adapter produce net depletions 425966524925658359 wstETH wei, 21426349774 USDC units, 1682081696577984059 WETH wei and 5195215318 USDT units; WBTC and aToken movements net to zero. Reproduce by filtering topic 0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef and summing amounts whose from/to is the execution address. This measures adapter residuals, not user-approved balances or flash-loan principal. The immutable AUGUSTUS_REGISTRY getter at creation is 0xa68bea62dc4034a689aa0f58a76681433caca663, ORACLE is 0x54586be62e3c3580375ae3723c145253060ca0c2, and POOL is 0x87870bca3f3fd6335c3f4ce8392d69350b4fa4e2. Unresolved: full campaign anchors/components and whether registry/ Augustus route history changed causal reachability after adapter deployment. Next: enumerate affected repay/debt-switch adapters and attacker transactions across the markets covered by source-9, compare runtime/failure identities before grouping, identify the earliest successful episode, reconcile all token depletion with the reported $95,284.44, and reconstruct registry/route activation history. No incident or target promotion. At Ethereum block 20624703, eth_call getAssetPrice(address), selector 0xb3596f07, for wstETH 0x7f39c581f595b53c5cb19bd0b3f8da6c935e2ca0 returns 291662772556; for WETH 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2 returns 247780486979. BASE_CURRENCY_UNIT() at that block returns 100000000. Stablecoin components use $1 par.

limitations: The full campaign extends beyond this Ethereum transaction to other repay and debt-switch adapters; earliest fault episode, cross-network component coverage and grouping remain unresolved.
The structured loss is an Ethereum lower bound; the final $95,284.44 project estimate has not been reconciled to full onchain components.
